invariant: Java factory selection treats each completed multiline command as one syntactic unit. For `note as N ... end note`, interior lines are opaque display text and cannot influence diagram type. Sequence rejects that opener, Class accepts it before Description is tried, and real commands after the terminator remain ordinary dispatch evidence. An unterminated note does not hide arbitrary remaining source.
causal_divergence: Rust independently scores every physical line. A note body beginning with `control` or `boundary` is counted as sequence/description syntax and can invalidate class viability, selecting Deployment even though the class parser already buffers the note body correctly. The deployment parser then interprets payload text as entities or produces an empty diagram.
planned_change: Classify completed multiline note spans before subtype scoring. Score the opener normally but exclude body and terminator lines from every subtype heuristic. Recognize command grammar rather than body keywords, and hide a span only when a valid terminator exists so malformed-input behavior and top-level commands after `end note` remain observable.
